steps.text: In bowl beat butter till creamy. Add brown sugar, cinnamon, and baking soda. Stir until combined. Mix in applesauce and egg. Add flour, a little at a time. Stir in oats.
Drop dough onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Applesauce Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy cookie recipe delivers oatmeal cookies made with applesauce.
raw_recipe.name: Applesauce Oatmeal Cookies

recipeInstructions.text: In bowl beat butter till creamy. Add brown sugar, cinnamon, and baking soda. Stir until combined. Mix in applesauce and egg. Add flour, a little at a time. Stir in oats.
Drop dough onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 8 to 10 minutes or until lightly browned. Enjoy!

review.reviewBody: People often forget to calculate sugar intake when they're thinking "healthy." Even non-diabetics need to watch their processed sugar inatake. If you really want this to be a healthy recipe, make sure you're using home-made or "natural" applesauce - regular store-bought applesauce has processed sugars in it. I'd cut down the brown sugar, too, although I know that takes away some of the YUM factor! You could try a natural sweetener like honey or apple juice concentrate, or use Stevia. Honey is great when you're baking with whole grains because the whole grain binds to the honey sugars and digests it differently - your body doesn't realize it's sugar. Just a few thoughts. Great cookies.

Solid 3.5 to 4 star rating, for what it's meant to be - which is a healthy, low-fat cookie. Keeping that in mind, I would definitely make it again, on a monthly or bi-monthly basis, so that I'll have some tasty AND easy-on-the-waistline treats available for those times when cookie cravings hit!

Based on the items in my pantry, reading other reviews, and my own preference for a less-sweet but still flavourful cookie, I made 6 changes: *to use 1/2 cup white sugar (because I had no brown sugar), *to use 1 tsp baking powder (because I had no baking soda), *to use 1/2 cup quick oats and 3/4 cup rolled oats, *to add 1 tsp vanilla, *to add 1 tsp cinnamon, *to add 1/2 tsp salt.

I refrigerated the dough for 15 minutes, then dropped them by the spoonful on a greased, lined cookie sheet, and baked for 12 minutes. (I rotated my cookie sheet after 6 minutes, to ensure even baking). In total, this made 40 bite-sized cookies (in 2 batches). They make a GREAT afternoon snack to go with a cuppa joe or tea. :) Try this, you won't regret it!

These were more like scones than cookies and yummy whilef being likely sweet and cakey. I also altered the recipe a bit:
- whole wheat flour (not white)
- 3/4 cup raisins
- 1/2 cup chopped nuts
- sucanat which is dried sugar cane (not brown sugar)

I used all-organic ingredients, maybe more for the psychological "yum" factor than anything else. :)

I made larger scoops (15 total) and baked for 12-15 minutes. 

In the future I might try to add some other things like nutmeg or something. Good base recipe.

I found this recipe looking for a somewhat healthy snack for my daughter to take to school to help her make it to her late lunch period. I wanted something that was satisfying but also with some nutritional value. I hate to buy prepackaged stuff like this because it's so hard to find a good one that doesn't break the bank. After reading some of the reviews and changes from others I added these changes as well and was very pleased with the results. If you are looking for a traditional sweet/treat oatmeal cookie this isn't the recipe for you. Here are the changes I made. I added 1/4 tsp. salt, 1/2 tsp. of vanilla extract, 1 heaping tablespoon of soaked flax seeds, and substituted 1/2 cup of white flour for whole wheat flour. I also baked them for 12 mins at 350. The next time I fix these (and I will, even my sugar crazed teen son liked them) I will add a few more nutrient rich ingredients like ground pecans,walnuts, or almonds to sneak into my kids. These types of recipes are good to hide healthy ingredients kids would normally turn their noses up to. Thanks for the recipe.
They turned out amazing! I included some Godiva Belgium mini chocolate chips and heath crumbles and they are to die for! 100% recommend for any occasion :) thank you for sharing!
Nice soft cookie, did make certain changes, used 1 cup Splenda instead of sugar, 1 tsp of baking soda, 1 tsp cinnamon, and 1tbsp of molasses. Baked at 350 for 12 min. Yummy, soft, chewy cookie.

This recipe makes great cookies! I'll be honest. I'm not very good at baking, but this recipe is easy and seems very forgiving. My cookies are crispy on the edges and bordering on a little bread-like in the middle. I added 2 teaspoons of cinnamon because I love the stuff, 2 tbsp of flax meal and 3 tbsp crushed almonds. Definitely the kind of cookie to play around with spices, nuts, and fruits.

I am giving this 5 stars as a low calorie cookie. If you don't care about calories there are definitely better cookies but for someone like me who wants to eat a cookie but not all the calories these are great. I did not have any real butter on hand as I mostly use Country Crock margarine with calcium so that's what I used in my version. I used unsweetened applesauce, ore than doubled the cinnamon ( I love cinnamon) and threw some craisins in it. Also added a tsp vanilla as other reviewers suggested. I really like them. They definitely taste healthier and make a great breakfast cookie. This amount made 12 good sized soft fluffy cookies. I am thinking might throw a banana in next time or maybe some banana extract. I will definitely be making these again....often.
I added more cinnamon, cardamom, vanilla, and salt as mentioned in another comment. Tasted delicious and moist. My son opted for fruit snack topping on his :).

The only issue that I have with this recipe is that it doesn't list how many raisins to add into the battter. I would like to know how much. I also found that it is good if one doesn't over-mix the batter. Be gentle with it!
Great little cookie as a healthier version of an oatmeal cookie. I added 1sp vanilla, 3/4 cup cranberries and about 1/2 cup chopped walnuts, my son loves them.
These cookies were very tasteless. Won't make that mistake again
Horrible bland taste, even added vanilla and raisins and still tasted like cardboard.
I enjoyed making this year ago, and I look frorward to making it again. This is a lightly sweet spice cookie. It's not high on spice burn and is aplesant snack too.
Loved it 😄
These are simple to made and freeze well. I do add M&M's or chocolate morsels for more flavor.

1/3 cup of dark brown sugar (that's what I had) and 1/2 cup raw honey. Added a little more flour and oats due to the honey. I also added about 6 oz of Chocolate chunks. I made 1/2 of them with vanilla extract and 1/2 without. I preferred the batch without the vanilla. I felt the chocolate chunks added enough flavor. I would make these again.
A good base recipe that can be modified for a variety of cookie types.

This recipe was puzzling. The photo showed raisins, but there were none in the ingredient list. I added them. I baked them for 13 minutes, and hubby said they needed another 3 to 5 minutes. They never spread and flattened. They didn't have much flavor, either. Pretty disappointing.
These awesome Applesauce Oatmeal Cookies are fantastic. They were really easy to prep and bake. I would make these again!
